tools_helpful.evidence: The bootstrap copied the source, preserved the UWP project reference, generated MIGRATION-MAPPING.md, and the required Test-Path check returned true near the start of session-log.txt.
Incremental builds exposed concrete namespace, import, color, and XAML errors; turn 61 ended with Build succeeded and 0 errors.
After an x64-specific rebuild, turn 69 classified the launch as crashed and captured System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException with the wrong-thread message.
Turn 70 returned only the startup-crashes section, including the WER event-log workflow used in the next turn.

tools_problematic.problem: Its target-mode layout resolver only searched bin\x64\Debug or bin\ARM64\Debug, so a normal default dotnet build under bin\Debug was reported as unavailable.
tools_problematic.evidence: Turn 65: status=unavailable, 'No build output found under bin\x64\Debug'; the tool only worked after turn 68 rebuilt with -p:Platform=x64.

tools_problematic.problem: The packaged launch surfaced only Arg_COMException, and diagnostic verbosity produced 11.4 MB without the actionable WER stack.
tools_problematic.evidence: Turns 64 and 75-76; the actionable exception appeared in Application event 1026 instead.

tool_limitations.limitation: The manifest checks covered desktop target, rescap, runFullTrust, and images but not the WinUI scaffold EntryPoint placeholder or a contradictory WindowsPackageType=None.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Fail when a retained Package.appxmanifest does not use EntryPoint="$targetentrypoint$" or the project suppresses packaging with WindowsPackageType=None.

tool_limitations.limitation: Layout discovery depended on an explicit Platform build and its generic CLR-exception hint did not recognize the specific Application.Start apartment message.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Discover the newest launchable layout recursively under bin and map the known message to the manifest entry-point invariant.

failed_apis.why_tried: The migrated status UI retained the UWP color helper while using a WinUI SolidColorBrush.
failed_apis.root_cause: Windows.UI.Colors was not available in the target projection.
failed_apis.fix: The agent replaced named colors with Color.FromArgb values in MainPage.xaml.cs.

doc_errors.wrong: The text said to treat WMC9999 as a dangling resource key rather than a code bug.
doc_errors.correct: WMC9999 is a cascade. Fix explicit CS#### and WMC#### errors first; audit resource keys only if WMC9999 remains alone.

special_apis.special_handling: The XAML control was replaced with MediaPlayerElement while the Windows.Media.Playback.MediaPlayer retained its MediaProtectionManager/PlayReady wiring through a small host object.
A packaged WinUI 3 app must retain the scaffold placeholder EntryPoint="$targetentrypoint$"; copying the UWP literal <Namespace>.App entry point can register and then crash in Application.Start.

errors_encountered.root_cause: Copied files mixed the UWP SDKTemplate namespace with the target PlayReady root namespace.
errors_encountered.fix: Normalize C# namespaces, XAML x:Class/xmlns declarations, and using directives to PlayReady.

errors_encountered.root_cause: Authored shell code referenced an unqualified dispatcher variable and then accidentally removed the Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls import.
errors_encountered.fix: Use _window.DispatcherQueue and restore the WinUI controls using directive.

errors_encountered.root_cause: The shell retained a UWP color helper that was not projected in the target.
A temporary UWP reference XAML file was copied into the SDK project's default compile glob.
The copied UWP manifest referenced branded assets that were not copied into the target.
errors_encountered.fix: Point manifest image attributes at the scaffold assets that exist.

errors_encountered.root_cause: Package.appxmanifest retained the UWP literal EntryPoint="PlayReady.App" instead of the WinUI scaffold EntryPoint="$targetentrypoint$".
errors_encountered.fix: Restore the WinUI entry-point placeholder; prevent recurrence with a validator check.

errors_encountered.error: winapp run found no package manifest in the final build output
errors_encountered.root_cause: The agent added <WindowsPackageType>None</WindowsPackageType> while retaining a packaged migration.
errors_encountered.fix: Remove WindowsPackageType=None for packaged projects and make the validator reject this contradiction.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: The agent retried packaged and unpackaged launches, rebuilt for x64, emitted a huge diagnostic log, inspected generated Main, and changed package type without fixing startup.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: Approximately 19 turns and four launch attempts.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: The manifest used a UWP literal application entry point, while validation did not enforce the already-documented WinUI placeholder.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Not resolved during migration; scoring confirmed the app remained unreachable.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Validate the Application EntryPoint and packaging-mode consistency before build/launch, and give the specific Application.Start apartment message a manifest-focused hint.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Test-AppLaunch reported no output after a successful default build, forcing another platform-specific build.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: One failed diagnostic and one extra build before retry.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Discover launchable layouts by their executable and AppxManifest.xml rather than by one path convention.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Several rebuilds were needed for namespace mismatches, accidentally removed imports, stale colors, and a temporary XAML file included in compilation.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: Roughly 21 turns before the first clean build.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: One-off editing mistakes and a temporary file placed under the project default glob.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: The compiler's specific errors were fixed sequentially and the temporary file was removed.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Follow the existing first-error build loop and keep reference artifacts outside the project compile tree.
